key_insight: Combining molecular sequence, 3D structure and biochemical features in a single multimodal deep learning model enables accurate, interpretable prediction of immunogenicity and supports targeted hypothesis generation.
problem_solved: Existing immunogenicity predictors are often single-modality and opaque; this work addresses the challenge of modelling the joint influence of sequence, structure and biochemical context while providing interpretable outputs for downstream design and validation.
method: Fuse three input modalities — amino-acid sequence, solved/predicted 3D structure, and biochemical/property descriptors — into a unified model.
Use modality-specific encoders with a joint integration layer and an interpretable prediction head (e.g., attention/attribution mechanisms) to map features to immunogenicity scores.

Produce both quantitative immunogenicity predictions and localized, interpretable attributions linking specific residues, structural regions or properties to predicted immune responses for hypothesis generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates how multimodal fusion plus interpretability can improve biological prediction tasks and accelerate experimental design (e.g., vaccine or therapeutic candidate prioritization) by surfacing testable mechanistic hypotheses.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing three input streams (sequence, structure, biochemical features) feeding into encoders and a joint prediction head
3D protein structure rendering with heatmap overlays highlighting residues/regions driving predicted immunogenicity
Comparison chart (e.g., bar or ROC curves) showing multimodal model vs unimodal baselines
Sequence motif map linked to structural view illustrating interpretable attribution (saliency/attention) back to residues
paper_title: ImmunoStruct enables multimodal deep learning for immunogenicity prediction
paper_authors: Kevin Bijan Givechian, João Felipe Rocha, Chen Liu, Edward Yang, Sidharth Tyagi
